_note: Seed lore fragments for Tansy, Poppy, Blue and their mother, first written 2026-10-23 from Dr. O's Human Summer spec. Fragments, never a chain: each one stands alone, each one is somebody's memory, and no two characters tell it the same way. Nobody knows what happened to the human. The first two examples under funny and emotional and the contradiction are Dr. O's own words.

fragments.text: According to Poppy, Tansy spent three days insisting she disliked the human while describing him in extraordinary detail.
Blue once found Tansy standing at the forest edge during the first spring rain. Neither spoke about why she was there.
No one knows what happened to the human after he left. Every fairy has a different theory.
Poppy claims Tansy still knows the exact date she met the human. Tansy refuses to confirm this.

Poppy: Tansy cried when he left.
Tansy: I absolutely did not.
Blue: There were tears.
Pretend all you want. Tansy kept a flower he gave her. FOR YEARS. It is in the second drawer, under the buttons, and she says it is research.
That summer changed Tansy forever. She learned that love and pride rarely survive together.
No daughter should lose her home without understanding the cost. One month was not a punishment. It was a door with a handle on both sides.
Did I ever love someone? That seems wildly personal. I did not say yes. I did not say anything. Please look at the buttons.
Two humans wandered into the woods once, a brother and a sister, loud, lost, and carrying a sandwich. It was entirely unremarkable. I remember it perfectly. That is a coincidence.
The human's sister and I were instantly best friends, she liked my hedgerow, I loved her hat. Tansy was very dignified about all of it for the first four minutes.
The elders still disagree about what became of him. Some say he was kept away. Some say he was lost. I only say that promises made in the woods are heavier than they look.
When she came home on the last day, I did not ask whether it hurt. I put the kettle on. A mother learns which questions are kindnesses.
My matchmaking record is excellent. I introduced two beetles at the midsummer picnic and they are, I think, still talking. Tansy says that was an ordinary conversation. I say they never stopped.
The festival of first dew requires everyone to wear a crown of clover. I wear mine under protest. Poppy wears hers to bed. Neither of these facts should leave this room.
A younger cousin asked me how to win an argument at Court. I told her to wait until the other person has finished being right. It took her three weeks to forgive me, and then it worked.
The Human Summer is the greatest love story ever told, and I will fight anyone who says otherwise, starting with my sister, who is standing right behind me looking at the ceiling.
Every spring, on one particular morning, Tansy is nowhere to be found until evening. She always comes back with dirt on her knees and an excellent excuse.
It is said Tansy once corrected a human's grammar for forty minutes. Poppy says the human was smiling the entire time. Tansy says that was not the reason she did it.

Humans are foolish. They carry heavy boxes for no reason. They say they are fine when they are not. They build a fire, then stand around it, when they could simply sit closer to it. I watched one for an hour once, for science.
There is a part of the forest the older fairies call the Quiet. The path to it never looks the same twice. Poppy went once and came back with a pocket full of acorns and no explanation.
I have kept the gate unlatched on that side for a long time. I tell the others it is a draft. I do not expect anyone to believe this.

Poppy: She still has the flower.
Tansy: It is a pressed specimen.
Blue: It has a ribbon on it.
People who say they will come back usually mean it when they say it. That is the part that interests me. That is the only part. Moving on.
